Once upon a time two mice were cousins.
Town Mouse lived in a big house in the city, and Country Mouse lived in a cosy hole in a field.
One day Town Mouse came to visit.
Country Mouse was so pleased that he gave her the best food he had.
Country Mouse brought out barley, a few nuts and a little bit of cheese.
Please eat, dear cousin,
said Country Mouse.
Town Mouse nibbled a nut and wrinkled her nose.
Is this all you have to eat?
said Town Mouse.
You must come and see how I live.
So the two mice set off to the city.
When they reached the big house, Town Mouse led Country Mouse into the dining room.
There was a long table with cakes, jelly, fruit and cheese.
Help yourself,
Country Mouse had never seen so much food.
What a feast!
You are so lucky to live here.
He was just about to take a bite of cake when the door burst open.
In came a big Cat, with sharp claws and green eyes.
Run!
The two mice dashed under the table and hid behind a cupboard.
They were trembling, and their hearts were beating very fast.
The cat padded away at last.
Is it always like this?
Oh, yes,
There is always a cat or a trap or a broom.
But the food is so good that it is worth it.
They crept out, but the door opened again, and in came the Cat's friend, a barking Dog.
Country Mouse had seen enough.
Thank you for the feast, cousin,
But I would rather have a nut in peace than a cake in fear.
Then go home, dear cousin,
I will stay here.
Country Mouse hurried back to his quiet field, and he was very glad to be home.
He ate his barley and nuts under the warm sun, and he had never tasted anything so good.
Simple food in peace is better than a feast in fear.
